walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Managing Business Activities — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Managing Business Activities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Managing Business Activities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an internal source of finance?
options: Retained profit
Bank overdraft
Share issue
Trade credit

mcqs.q: Profit can differ from cash flow because:
options: Sales made on credit count toward profit before the cash actually arrives
Cash flow is always higher than profit
Profit measures the money in the till each day
Cash and profit are identical for all businesses
Actual output minus break-even output
Break-even output minus actual output
Fixed costs minus variable costs
Revenue minus total contribution

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Overdrafts can only be used to pay tax bills.
Profitable businesses are automatically taken over by the government.
Because it can run out of cash — profit counts credit sales immediately, but if cash arrives too late to pay wages and suppliers, the business becomes insolvent.
If a business makes a profit it cannot collapse.

mcqs.q: Is an overdraft a good source of long-term finance?
options: Profitable businesses are automatically taken over by the government.
An overdraft is the cheapest way to fund any business need.
Overdrafts can only be used to pay tax bills.
No — overdrafts are flexible for short-term cash gaps but carry high interest and are repayable on demand; long-term needs suit loans or share capital better.

mcqs.q: Does break-even analysis give a precise, reliable answer?
options: The break-even chart tells a business exactly how many units it will sell.
Break-even analysis applies only to airlines.
Overdrafts can only be used to pay tax bills.
Only as a simplification — it assumes all output is sold, costs behave linearly and the price stays constant, so real outcomes often differ from the chart.
